A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with SELFEE renamed SPA in v2. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, AlpacaEval 2.0 and MT-Bench measurements, and qualitative outputs in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds seed-data sensitivity experiments, additional model evaluations, and length-regularization and judge-initialization controls.

M1.justification: The core procedure in Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–12 is unchanged apart from renaming and clarification. However, v2 Appendix D adds an evaluated optional variant that subtracts a length penalty from rewards during preference labeling, changing that variant's label-generation procedure.

E1.justification: UltraChat/UltraFeedback training coverage and AlpacaEval 2.0/MT-Bench evaluation tasks are retained. The additional backbones and seed-data quantities change model configurations and sample sizes, rather than task or domain coverage. The scenario without seed preference data already appears in v1.

E2.justification: Zephyr-7b-alpha is removed from Table 1, while v2 Table 11 adds an LLM-as-judge variant initialized from the preceding iteration's model. The principal DPO, PairRM, and fixed LLM-as-judge comparators remain. Zephyr-7b-beta's revised training is a settings change, rather than a new comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation settings through seed-size sweeps with fixed iteration prompts, seed-dataset resampling, and LLaMA-3-8B/Phi-3-14B experiments with specified learning-rate, beta, and epoch adjustments. Appendix B.2 describes reimplementing Zephyr-7b-beta with the SFT model and cleaned preference data matched to SPA. Table 2 also replaces v1's no-refinement proposed variant with full SPA, reducing isolation of the preference-judgment component in that comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond retained component and reference-model ablations, v2 adds sensitivity to seed-data quantity and sampling, tests whether length penalties mitigate verbosity, and controls whether updating the LLM-as-judge initializer explains SPA's advantage. Table 9 extends MT-Bench ablation evidence with the no-self-refinement result. These address several substantive robustness and mechanism questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 newly reports results across three sampled seed datasets, with averages and variances; v1 has no corresponding statistics. The accompanying text invokes a confidence-interval lower bound without specifying its confidence level or construction. This is limited new uncertainty reporting, not a documented increase from a previously specified replication count.

E6.justification: Headline SELFEE/SPA results remain 15.39% length-controlled win rate, 21.13% ordinary win rate, and 6.94 MT-Bench score. Zephyr-7b-beta changes from 13.2%/11% to 11.75%/10.03% under revised training, so these are replacement results. Numerous seed, backbone, and control results are added. Table 10 shows the new length penalty reducing iteration-two output length from 2749 to 2448 characters while lowering length-controlled win rate from 16.23% to 14.46%. Several earlier response-length entries are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds the mathematical definition of the length-penalized reward in Appendix D, Equation 13. This is a limited formal addition; the original preference definitions, DPO derivation, refinement equations, and extrapolation relationship remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Despite the new title and acronym, both versions claim efficient alignment through intrinsic preference judgment and noise-aware self-refinement using little labeled preference data. Claims of baseline superiority, applicability across LLMs, and operation without seed preference data are retained. The added experiments support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 elaborates the distribution-shift explanation for fixed reward models' weaker iterative performance and adds interpretations concerning seed robustness, compatibility with length control, and the judge-initialization control. The verbosity limitation is retained and relocated to Appendix A; it is not newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 adds checkpoint identifiers and training settings for LLaMA-3/Phi-3, documents the revised Zephyr comparison and length-penalty coefficient range, and supplies a project-code URL plus a code/checkpoint release statement. Hardware, runtime estimates, the 300-token generation cap, and the 50-sample confidence calculation were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SimPO, LLaMA 3, RLHFlow, and Chen et al.'s implicit-reward bootstrapping work. It explicitly distinguishes the latter's length-regularization focus from SPA's self-refinement focus. These are limited additions to otherwise retained research positioning, rather than a wholesale related-work revision.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, renames SELFEE to SPA, updates affiliation and publication text, and makes localized prose clarifications. It reorganizes experimental analyses, moves limitations into Appendix A, and adds a reproducibility statement. Most introductory and methodological prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: MT-Bench scores are integrated into the main comparison tables, response-length columns are removed from several retained tables, the model-comparison table is expanded, and new sensitivity/control tables are added. Figures 2 and 4 reorder metric groups, Figure 3 drops the no-refinement curve, and the document adopts the ICLR layout. Qualitative examples remain unchanged apart from labels and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical credibility through seed-sensitivity checks, additional backbones, a better-matched Zephyr comparison, and targeted length and judge-initialization controls. These improve support for the retained findings. The gains are tempered by unexplained confidence-interval language, removal of several response-length measurements, and the less controlled headline judgment comparison in Table 2, although the no-refinement ablation remains available elsewhere.
